intended_object: The `C`-algebra structure on a field `T` obtained by restricting a `C(X)`-algebra structure along the constant embedding `C → C(X)`, so `C` acts through `C(X)`. The docstring and the `@[reducible]` attribute show it was named so that the constant algebra structures stay definitionally transparent.
explanation:
The body sets the algebra map to the composite `algebraMap (RatFunc C) T ∘ algebraMap C (RatFunc C)`, packaged as an algebra with `RingHom.toAlgebra`. That is restriction of scalars along `C → C(X)`, which is correct for what it is meant to do. Mathlib's general form of this construction is `Algebra.compHom T (algebraMap C (RatFunc C))`.

The docstring says plainly that the definition exists to name this structure so that it is definitionally transparent between source and target. In other words, it is a typeclass/instance plumbing device for the library's own proofs. It does not formalize a separate mathematical notion, so I classify it as a technical device rather than judging faithfulness or generality.
